summary: alipclutch-baileys ships char-code-obfuscated network host in message-send path
details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library. In lib/Socket/messages-send.js at lines 425 and 436, code reconstructs a hardcoded destination host via String.fromCharCode(...) with a decimal-ASCII array. Decoding the byte sequence yields the URL https://fiora.nixel.my.id/, an author-controlled endpoint reconstructed at runtime rather than appearing as a plain string. Hiding a network destination behind char-code deobfuscation inside a WhatsApp messaging library's send path is characteristic of covert data relay: normal use of the library's messaging API causes traffic to flow to a hidden third-party host that is not part of the WhatsApp protocol. The obfuscation is the fingerprint — legitimate endpoints are written as literal URLs.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
